title: Client IP is taken from client-controllable forwarded headers (leftmost X-Forwarded-For, unconditional CF-Connecting-IP)
test: tests/requestIdentity.test.js: 'VAL-132: behind a SHARE_BASE_URL proxy a client-supplied CF-Connecting-IP never chooses the client', 'VAL-146: CF-Connecting-IP is read for Nextra's own running tunnel and under TRUST_CLOUDFLARE_CONNECTING_IP only', 'the rate-limit bucket of a relay forwarded headers do not cover comes from CF-Connecting-IP only under a Cloudflare mode'; tests/forwardedClientIdentity.test.js (new): 'the socket handlers' own IP fallback skips the TRUST_PROXY hop count and honours only the explicit Cloudflare flag', 'the WHEP router's own IP fallback skips the TRUST_PROXY hop count and honours only the explicit Cloudflare flag', and three real-server tests: 'VAL-132 on the real server: behind a SHARE_BASE_URL proxy a client-supplied CF-Connecting-IP never names the client', 'VAL-146 on the real server: TRUST_CLOUDFLARE_CONNECTING_IP=true gives each Cloudflare viewer its own identity', 'VAL-146 on the real server: Nextra's own quick tunnel reads CF-Connecting-IP, other loopback relays do not' (a stand-in cloudflared: CLOUDFLARED_PATH is node, which runs a 'tunnel' script from the server's working directory that prints a trycloudflare URL); tests/network.test.js: 'getCloudflareClientIp returns CF-Connecting-IP only when it is one valid address'
proof: Holds in part after TASK-005 (e640d25): X-Forwarded-For was already read from the right with the TRUST_PROXY hop count and CF-Connecting-IP only under trustCloudflareClientIp, but lib/requestIdentity.js set that for any loopback request addressed to a known share URL, which includes a SHARE_BASE_URL the operator set for nginx or Caddy; its fallback also named the rate-limit bucket 'public-share:<CF-Connecting-IP>' for any loopback relay with Cloudflare headers; and the fallback resolvers getSocketIp (lib/socket.js) and getRequestIp (lib/whepRoutes.js) ignored TRUST_PROXY. On the unchanged code (dev 482d5d6): a real server with SHARE_BASE_URL=https://stream.example.com answered GET /api/package-info (local-only) with 200 instead of 403 for Host stream.example.com, X-Forwarded-For 203.0.113.180 and CF-Connecting-IP 127.0.0.1 ('200 !== 403'); getClientIpFromHeaders returned '127.0.0.1' instead of the proxy-appended '203.0.113.20'; a second client behind two proxies with TRUST_PROXY=2 was rate-limited on join-room and on WHEP POST (429 !== 404) because both fallbacks keyed on the outer proxy; with Nextra's quick tunnel running, a loopback relay not addressed to the tunnel got a new join bucket for each CF-Connecting-IP ('Room not found.' where 'Too many attempts' was expected); TRUST_CLOUDFLARE_CONNECTING_IP=true had no effect ('second viewer was rate-limited'). Failing output: dev-notes/results/TASK-094-before.txt (the real-server flag test there was run again after it was changed to a setup without SHARE_BASE_URL; its first version passed on the old code because any share URL counted). Now CF-Connecting-IP names the client only for a loopback request addressed to the tunnel Nextra launched while it is active (server.js getManagedTunnelOrigin: status 'active', quick or named) or with TRUST_CLOUDFLARE_CONNECTING_IP=true (config.js, default false, README and .env.example), only as one valid address; with neither, a CF-only relayed request is still 'unknown' (remote) and an unproven relay shares the bucket 'public-share-proxy'; the fallbacks pass the hop count and the flag. All new tests pass; the network, operatorBoundary, publicLinkOperatorBoundary and serverIntegration tests pass. Two existing expectations in tests/requestIdentity.test.js depended on the defect and were changed: the identity() fixture now declares its trycloudflare share URL as Nextra's running tunnel (getManagedTunnelOrigin), and VAL-079's 'untrusted' case expects 'public-share-proxy' instead of 'public-share:203.0.113.9'.
